app/orchestration/tasks/base.py.summary: TaskContext gains an additive `ephemeral: bool = False` field marking a synthetic per-child fan-out task that must not create a durable Job row or queue.items broadcast.

app/orchestration/tasks/segment_synthesi.summary: _SyntheticSegmentTask.describe() sets ephemeral=True. ChapterSynthesisTask._publish_progress now also computes a size-weighted, order-independent grouped_progress ratio from each child's in-memory group["text_length"] and threads it through the existing grouped_progress kwarg; run() tracks done_chars/total_chars across child completions.

app/orchestration/scheduler/orchestrator.summary: _publish() early-returns before any durable job-state/broadcast work when context.ephemeral is True, so per-child fan-out contexts never create a phantom Job row or fire queue.items/jobs.lifecycle broadcasts.

app/db/segments.py.summary: New chapter_completion_by_size(chapter_id) -> (done_chars, total_chars) query helper, size-weighted via LENGTH(text_content), audio_status='done' as the completion value.

tests/orchestration/test_ephemeral_child.summary: New test: a chapter fan-out (cap=1 and cap=2) produces exactly one durable Job row (the parent), zero {parent}-seg-N phantom child rows.

tests/orchestration/test_grouped_progres.summary: New test: a 900-char segment completing before a 100-char sibling reports grouped_progress ~= 0.9 (size-weighted, order-independent), not ~0.5 (count-based).

design-docs/specs/queue-jobs.md.summary: spec_version 1.10.0 -> 1.11.0; documents ephemeral TaskContext suppression of durable child job rows and size-weighted grouped_progress.

design-docs/specs/live-events.md.summary: spec_version 1.9.3 -> 1.9.4; documents groupedProgress now being populated by the chapter fan-out and ephemeral contexts no longer emitting any frame via _publish.

wiki/Changelog.md.summary: Dated 2026-07-04 Fix entry for the ephemeral child job-row suppression and size-weighted chapter completion.

flow_impact: Chapter fan-out now produces exactly one durable Job row per chapter render (parent only) regardless of segment count or concurrency cap, and chapter-level completion percentage is weighted by rendered text size rather than segment count, correctly reflecting out-of-order completion of unequal-size segments.
